claim: The symbol detector finds nearly all symbols on held-out sheets
evidence: experiment_log: kaggle_v1 sheet-level evaluation; TEST RESULTS
result: Test: precision 0.9999, recall 1.0000 (9,105 TP, 1 FP, 0 FN)
limitations: Synthetic, clean, evenly balanced data; says nothing about real drawings

claim: End-to-end tag reading is the weak link
result: Test end-to-end tag exact 61.6% vs 89.0% when reading ground-truth word boxes (tuning sheets)
limitations: Tag reading tuned on validation sheets 3 and 5; allowlist from the dataset's own character set

claim: Without abstention, extraction errors make the verifier declare every matching pair non-conforming (H1)
result: Test: 75/75 matching pairs FAIL; 20,978 false vs 456 true findings

claim: OCR confidence alone does not make automatic decisions trustworthy
evidence: experiment_log: decide_v1 rule A; TEST RESULTS
result: Test risk 24.0% at tau 0.98 (baseline 25.0%); risk reaches 0% only when no text is trusted (17.0% coverage)
limitations: EasyOCR confidence only; other OCR engines not tested

claim: Combining OCR confidence with format plausibility lowers the risk of automatic decisions while deciding about half the cases (H2)
evidence: experiment_log: decide_v1 rule B; TEST RESULTS; src/bootstrap_ci.py
result: Test at frozen tau 0.98: coverage 52.3% [46.3, 58.3], risk 6.4% [3.1, 9.6] vs 25.0% without abstention
limitations: Rule B designed after rule A failed on validation; formats learned from regular synthetic tags; 75 test sheets

claim: The decision rule meets a 5% risk target on unseen data
result: Test risk 6.4% (interval 3.1 to 9.6); 4.0% on validation where tau was chosen

claim: The system can certify conforming drawings automatically
result: 0 of 75 matching pairs passed automatically at any tau, on validation or test
limitations: Every sheet contains some reading the rule does not trust

claim: The trade-off generalises from validation to test
result: Coverage 50.3% (val) vs 52.3% (test); risk 4.0% vs 6.4%
limitations: Same synthetic generator for both splits

claim: Detection transfers to real plant drawings
evidence: experiment_log: open100_v1 (12 real OPEN100 plans, post hoc)
result: At matched scale (4x): coarse-label recall 0.834, precision 0.676 (vs 0.9999 on synthetic test); native scale much worse; 10% of real symbols belong to classes absent from training
limitations: 12 plans; coarse labels only; scale chosen from annotations; no text, so tag reading and verification untested on real drawings
use_in_paper: with caveat (as qualitative evidence and a limitation)

claim: Calibrated confidence beats the raw detector score (H3)
result: Not tested before the test run
limitations: Any later analysis is post hoc

claim: Graph reasoning improves verification
result: Not justified for this task: at most 11.1% of tag errors are association errors connectivity could address; 74.1% are misreads and 14.8% no text found; only 2 involved line labels
limitations: Benchmark has no connectivity discrepancies, so no full ablation is possible; upper bound inflated by repeated size texts
use_in_paper: yes, as a negative finding and future work

claim: VLM assistance improves verification
result: Not evaluated

claim: A reproducible paired drawing-BOM benchmark with failing cases
result: 2,000 cases; byte-identical regeneration; oracle verifier 2,000/2,000 verdicts correct
limitations: Synthetic discrepancies on the BOM side only; source dataset licence unclear, so images cannot be redistributed

claim: No prior work implements and measures verification of raster P&IDs against an independent BOM with abstention
result: Targeted literature search found none; Chen and Cheng (2026) propose abstention without an implementation; Youn et al. (2026) need CAD files
limitations: Search was targeted, not exhaustive; re-check before submission

claim: The pipeline runs on a CPU-only laptop
result: Detection about 20 s and extraction about 27 s per sheet on an Intel i5-10300H with 8 GB RAM
limitations: Training needed a GPU (10 h on a Kaggle T4)

claim: The format check cannot reveal the symbol class
result: Letters map to A and digits to 9 before comparison
limitations: Format lengths still differ between some class groups

claim: Confidence and format plausibility are each insufficient; their combination is what lowers risk
result: Test AURC: rule A 0.154, rule B 0.090, paired difference 0.064 [0.051, 0.080]; format only at no threshold: coverage 94.7%, risk 23.2%
limitations: Computed after the test run from frozen outputs; no setting changed

claim: REVIEW cases still need substantial human checking
result: Rule B REVIEW cases: median 56.7% of components untrusted (test), median 66 flagged findings
limitations: No user study of review time

claim: A reader trained on the pipeline's own text crops raises end-to-end tag reading and the coverage of trustworthy automatic decisions
evidence: experiment_log: reader_v2b; TEST RESULTS v2b; src/compare_runs.py
result: Test: tag exact 87.7% vs 61.6%; rule B coverage 64.0% [59.3, 68.7] vs 52.3%, risk 4.2% [1.6, 6.8]; paired coverage +11.7 points [5.3, 17.7], AURC -0.035 [-0.047, -0.023]; risk change not significant
limitations: Second, disclosed look at the test sheets (protocol and configuration committed beforehand); synthetic data

claim: Reader accuracy on clean word crops does not predict accuracy inside the pipeline
result: Reader trained on ground-truth boxes: 99.8% on them, 77.9% on pipeline crops; end-to-end 69.4%; rule B at tau 0.98 risk 13.6% (validation)
